questions.q: The position of the vertical LRAS curve shows:
options: The normal capacity level of output
questions.why: It's what the economy can sustainably produce.

questions.q: Which is a fundamental determinant of LRAS?
questions.why: Others include productivity, attitudes, enterprise, factor mobility and incentives.

questions.q: How can the banking system affect aggregate supply?
options: By providing funds for business investment
questions.why: Investment adds to the capital stock.

questions.q: On the Keynesian AS curve, at full capacity, a rise in AD only raises prices.
Match each part of the Keynesian AS curve to what a rise in AD does.
questions.why: It depends on how much spare capacity there is.

questions.q: Explain how a rise in investment could affect both aggregate demand and long-run aggregate supply.

ideas.label: Investment is a part of AD, so AD rises
More capital raises productive capacity, so LRAS shifts right

questions.model: Investment is a part of AD, so AD rises in the short run. It also adds to the capital stock, which raises productive capacity and shifts LRAS to the right.
questions.why: Investment works on both sides of the diagram.

tests.answer: Investment is part of AD so AD rises, and it adds to capacity so LRAS shifts right.
